ac:layout-cell.h1: Customer Onboarding and Connectivity Solution Summary
ac:layout-cell.p: Solution Summary · Logical Feature Specification · Sequence and Reuse Assessment · Folder

This view combines SPEC-SEI-018 onboarding and SPEC-SEI-034 connection setup. It keeps their scope and decisions. The summary and diagram now show the main journey; SPEC038 holds the required behaviour and SPEC039 the existing E-Invoice API reuse decisions. Archived sources are unchanged. Provider support, operator approval and actual Spain implementation remain open.
What: let a business or its authorised accountant set up Sage access to its chosen supported e-invoicing platform. Show what is ready, what is missing and who must act next.
Why: use existing accounts, valid certificates and working connections without repeating setup or accidentally changing provider.

Customer interaction: use one E-invoicing settings area to review setup and choose Connect or add a platform, Switch platform or Disconnect or stop a service. A switch is one customer request; Sage coordinates the new setup and any old-service exit. SPEC038 — E-invoicing settings defines the intended interaction and enabled-action limits.

Reuse: use the existing E-Invoice API and Tax certificate capability. Confirm Spain service settings, NIF/address rules, permissions, certificate acceptance and provider support. The API was first used for France; it is shared.
Product precondition: integrate SXS and Tax certificate management before enabling e-invoicing; see the shared rule in 038.

Read next: SPEC038 explains behaviour, ERP/Domain Service handoffs and exceptions; its §7 mapping links those functional actions to the sequences in SPEC039. SPEC039 gives calls, reuse recommendations and required changes; 040 holds API examples. These drafts do not prove production support.

The intended settings area lives in the business's Sage product or the accountant's Sage product, for the selected business or client. Guided onboarding, where provided, uses the same setup journey; see SPEC038 §1 — entry points. The exact menu location and screen design remain to agree with the product team.
Editable settings overview · PNG.

This is the primary specification home of the e-invoicing-settings-actions diagram. Its shared files stay in assets/diagrams/. SPEC038 — E-invoicing settings owns the settings behaviour. SPEC038 — Switch platform owns the complete customer switch journey. SPEC032 owns exit checks within that journey. SPEC014 — Routing controls owns the controlled change for future invoices. Offboarding references this overview rather than maintaining a second settings flow.
Use the shared glossary.

ac:layout-cell.p: These scenarios can overlap. SPEC038 — Scenario table owns their required behaviour. Figure 1 applies the relevant paths to the requested functions; a scenario ID does not select an exclusive branch.

Phase coverage: 1 — SPFE public solution; 2 — external private providers; 3 — Sage private-platform offering. Labels show analysis coverage, not delivery approval or confirmed API availability. REF-PHASE. Public checks remain relevant in Phases 2–3. Private A to Private B stays disabled. A customer may act directly or through an authorised accountant; one client needs no batch mode.

Onboarding does not send an invoice, assume public enrolment or prove operator eligibility. Sending, receiving, reporting and full exit stay in their owning features. Sage acting as a private platform requires separate operator approval under REF-OPERATOR.

Pending checks, unknown effects and unanswered actions remain open. Rejection/withdrawal records the requested work's outcome; cancellation completes only after possible external effects are resolved. Existing service and earlier obligations keep their own status.

Timing: customer setup has no general 30-day promise. An applicable platform-operator interconnection request has a one-month receiving-operator period, with the specific queue exception and required interim public exchange. SPEC038 operator handoff gives the exact rule. REF-INTERCONNECT.

ac:layout-cell.p: The product integration precondition is a separate note above the customer flow. Open E-invoicing settings or guided onboarding, Select the business or client, Review current e-invoicing setup, then Choose the requested action. SPEC038 — ONB-01 owns this interaction. ONB-10 defines the SXS dataset mapping, saved setup lookup and display, and missing/unavailable lookup outcomes. Saved setup does not prove readiness.

Colour key: light teal marks Customer settings, including guided onboarding screens, where the customer selects, reviews and sees results. Light purple marks Setup and checks, the onboarding/configuration work for the selected action. The product precondition stays neutral grey. These colours identify activity type; they do not indicate implementation, readiness or success. Both groups remain in one journey.

Figure 1. Which platform setup applies? selects the public and/or private paths. Both reuse valid setup and evidence; complete only missing, changed or expired work under ONB-10. Their results lead to the same Start or change platform use? decision. No — setup only returns results without activating or changing any platform selection. Yes follows the enabled, authorised choice and agreed start under ONB-07. The SPEC038 detailed swimlane expands this journey into four stages and shows the actor handoffs.

The private path asks Account on chosen private platform? Existing accounts need a Sage connection or valid connection reuse; a new account needs provider onboarding and connection. Prior use of another provider does not answer that question. ONB-05 defines both cases and the evidence needed for the provider's onboarding process. The confirmed NIF and certificate reuse rule applies across platforms; each added platform still needs separate connection setup (onboarding).

An authorised accountant follows this same flow for the selected client. The platform account and authority must cover that client; the firm's own account is not a default substitute. Missing client approval follows ONB-12. A single client needs no batch; ONB-13 adds isolated processing when a client list is requested.

Each E reference leads to Show pending result or limitation, with recovery under ONB-08. Missing SXS mapping follows the qualified setup process; an unavailable lookup is not proof of missing setup. Failed dependencies block only affected work. Phase 1 covers public access; Phases 2–3 add private setup and enabled platform changes. The diagram does not select the Spain API resource model; see 039 GAP-02. Draw.io · PNG.

ac:layout-cell.p: Keep Spain rules separate from shared behaviour and keep test/production evidence separate. An added function rechecks only its affected requirements; working setup remains unchanged.

Reuse decisions belong to SPEC039. Reuse of a design is not proof of running code. Confirm Tax certificate acceptance for each selected action. DTS remains the preferred conversion candidate for later invoice features under SPEC008; onboarding converts no invoice. Peppol is outside this scope.

ac:layout-cell.h2: 10 Features within this Master Feature — Phases 1–3
ac:layout-cell.p: Onboarding owns customer setup and its recovery. Certificate, connectivity/routing and invoice-operation features keep their responsibilities. SPEC038 links their handoffs. Configured account, readiness, route activation and operator approval remain separate results; no new deployment boundary is approved.
Before enabling work, close its functional/release checks in SPEC038 and implementation checks in SPEC039.
